title: What space does to your body
caption:
Good news: you won't explode in space. Bad news: everything else. 🚀
With no air pressure, the water in your body boils even at 37°C; your skin swells but holds, and you'd pass out in about 10 to 15 seconds.
Would you risk the shortcut?
sources: NASA Ask an Astrophysicist / NASA Goddard, human body in a vacuum (no explosion; ebullism; ~10-15 s of useful consciousness)
NASA Manned Spacecraft Center, 1966 vacuum chamber accident (Jim LeBlanc: saliva bubbling; repressurised within seconds; survived)
